title: spec review: Active path 3: handoff-aware executor routing (start strong when expected route cost says so) within pool constraints
spec:
Today (T-0831) [handoff] mode "active" is treated as shadow: executor.start records a "handoff" decision with expected_route_cost per eligible executor but launches the baseline pick. Build the active branch. Facts: executor.start picks via pool.pick_executor + allocation (executor.py ~276-323); handoff_scorecard.expected_route_cost(task_class, executor, root, cfg) returns a number or {"insufficient": True}; promotion CRITERIA min_samples 20.
Do:
1. Active: after the baseline pick, when every eligible executor has sufficient samples for the task's class and the lowest expected_route_cost executor differs from the baseline by more than [handoff] min_gain (new key, default 0.15 = 15% cheaper expected cost-to-accept), launch that executor instead; record the decision row with selected = the chosen executor and reason "expected_route_cost" plus the gain; otherwise keep the baseline with reason "insufficient_evidence" or "gain_below_threshold". Hard pool constraints (eligibility, cooldowns, complexity ceilings such as Astra for ≥9, budgets) stay authoritative: the router only chooses among pool.eligible_executors.
2. Cap: at most [handoff] max_active_share (default 0.5) of the day's execute launches may deviate from the baseline, so the baseline keeps producing comparison data; count per day in pool_state or the decision log.
3. Outcome feedback: when a task started under an active handoff decision reaches merged or failed, decision_log.outcome(task, "handoff", ...) records rounds, accepted tokens and usd; handoff_scorecard.by_start already aggregates by first executor, add a column "active_share".
Tests: tests/test_executor.py::test_active_handoff_switches_executor_when_gain_exceeds_threshold, ::test_active_handoff_keeps_baseline_without_evidence, ::test_active_share_cap_enforced; tests/test_handoff_scorecard.py::test_active_outcome_rows_feed_by_start; docs/context-economy/08-handoffs.md Active section with the revert path ([handoff] mode shadow).
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.
acceptance: docs/context-economy/08-handoffs.md has an Active section; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

risks.issue: Spec item 3 requires firing decision_log.outcome('handoff', ...) 'when a task started under an active handoff decision reaches merged or failed', but daemon.py has no single insertion point for that: failed status is posted from at least 8 separate bus.post_result(task_id, ..., "failed") call sites (lines ~548,559,568,616,617,625,629,632) plus more in executor.py, and merged_into is set in a different set of places (~1385-1391, 1528). The spec names the file but not which of these transitions to hook, so the executor must either duplicate the outcome call at every site (error-prone, likely to miss one and silently under-report) or invent a new centralized hook outside the stated scope.

by_start() currently aggregates purely from bus tasks/runs (_tasks()/_runs()) and never reads the decision log. Adding an 'active_share' column requires knowing, per lineage, whether its first dispatch was an active handoff switch (selected != baseline) — data that only exists in decision_log 'handoff' rows, which this module doesn't currently read or import. The spec doesn't say whether to (a) scan schedlog decisions and join by task id, or (b) stamp a field on the bus task at dispatch time and read it the way _tasks() already does. Left unspecified, the join is likely to be built inconsistently with the existing task-file-based aggregation and the acceptance test test_active_outcome_rows_feed_by_start could pass against an incomplete/mismatched join.

The three allowed decision reasons ('expected_route_cost' to switch, 'insufficient_evidence' and 'gain_below_threshold' to keep baseline) don't cover the max_active_share cap case: an executor can have sufficient samples and gain above min_gain, yet still be kept on baseline solely because the daily active-share cap is full. Without a distinct reason (e.g. 'cap_reached'), test_active_share_cap_enforced can't distinguish 'capped' from 'gain too low' from the decision row, and by_start/active_share analytics would conflate the two.

The spec's day-scoped max_active_share counter ('count per day in pool_state or the decision log') has no locking requirement, but the codebase's only existing atomic daily-state pattern is Pool's reservation-file mutate() closure used by reserve() (pool.py ~301); Pool itself has no lock around save(), and decision_log._append just appends a JSONL line with no read-check-write guard. daemon.py can dispatch multiple ready tasks concurrently, so a naive 'count today's active decisions then compare to cap' implementation can race and overshoot max_active_share silently (two concurrent start() calls both read the same under-cap count before either records their decision).

The handoff block runs after the existing allocation-active override (line 315-316: ex = pool.executors[choice['executor']]), so 'baseline' as read into the handoff decision may already be allocation's active pick, not pool.pick_executor's raw output. Spec point 1 says 'hard pool constraints stay authoritative' but doesn't address ordering/precedence between two evidence-based active layers (allocation and handoff) if both are active simultaneously — a handoff switch would silently discard an already-active allocation decision without recording that interaction.

suggested_spec_changes: Item 3: name the exact daemon.py hook point(s) for merged/failed outcome recording, or specify a single wrapper (e.g. around bus.post_result / the merge helper) rather than leaving 'daemon.py' as the scope with no site named.

Item 3 / by_start: specify whether active_share is computed by having executor.py stamp a field on the bus task row at dispatch time (consistent with handoff_scorecard._tasks() already reading task fields) versus scanning decision_log and joining by task id.
Add a fourth decision reason (e.g. 'cap_reached') for when gain and evidence would justify a switch but max_active_share blocks it, so cap enforcement is auditable from the decision log alone.

Point the day-counter at the existing atomic reservation-file mutate() pattern in pool.py (or equivalent lock) instead of leaving 'pool_state or the decision log' unspecified, to avoid a race that overshoots max_active_share under concurrent dispatch.

Clarify precedence when both [allocation] and [handoff] are active: should handoff's baseline be pool.pick_executor's raw pick or the post-allocation ex, and should a handoff switch be allowed to override an active allocation decision?
